title: Customer Advocacy Liaison: Escalation Runway & Signal-to-Roadmap Gate
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a repeatable program and decision gate that turns high-touch customer advocacy and escalation signals into prioritized, time-boxed roadmap commitments or fallbacks. This ticket captures the liaison cadence, a quantifiable escalation runway, and the signal-to-roadmap gating rubric used by PMs and Sales/CS to turn requests into scoped work or a formal decline with compensating actions.
background: Multiple strategic accounts have asked for roadmap commitments with varying urgency and legal implications. Engineering and Sales have inconsistent expectations about when an escalation becomes a committed deliverable vs an exploration. Lack of a predictable process causes missed SLAs, frustrated customers, and ad-hoc feature work that derails planned cycles.
goals: Define a clear liaison role and cadence between PM, AE/CS, and engineering for top-account escalations
Create an "escalation runway" algorithm that translates customer signals (deal size, legal exposure, usage patterns, time-to-value) into a recommended commitment window and prioritization tier
Ship a signal-to-roadmap gate checklist and acceptance criteria to remove ambiguity and reduce unilateral commitments
proposed_solution: Introduce a Customer Advocacy Liaison (CAL) playbook: a one-page rubric + a lightweight intake form. The rubric scores requests on five axes (commercial impact, technical feasibility, customer urgency, security/compliance risk, and support burden). Score -> escalation runway mapping recommends: Triage (watchlist), Advisory (engineering scoping), Committed (in roadmap within N cycles), or Enterprise SLA path (requires contract amendment). The PM owning the feature must complete a Gate Review doc; engineering provides initial feasibility estimate and must identify a fallback plan (compatible model variant, feature flag, or temporary workaround).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form live in Confluence and linked from CS playbook
Escalation runway algorithm documented with worked examples for small, mid, and enterprise deals
Gate checklist template created and used in two pilot escalations with documented decisions
All pilot escalations result in either a scoped roadmap entry with cycle target or a formal decline with compensating actions and customer communication draft

success_metrics: Reduction in unplanned high-priority engineering work tied to escalations by 60% within 2 cycles
Time from escalation intake to decision reduced to <= 10 business days
>80% satisfaction score from CS/AEs on clarity of outcome after pilot runs
Measured increase in accurate release commitments for enterprise accounts (commitment hit rate > 90%)
customer_signals: Contract amendment requests referencing roadmap commitments
Escalation tickets opened with legal/compliance tags
Repeated high-latency or error-rate incidents affecting SLA-reliant customers
Direct AE/CS asks for new capabilities tied to renewal timelines
risks: Over-indexing on high-dollar accounts could skew roadmap away from product-market fit
Customers may expect faster delivery windows than engineering can safely promise
Mis-scored requests could create repeated rework and erosion of trust
out_of_scope: Any requests for general usability improvements not tied to strategic account escalations and requests that are solely for experimental research prototypes.
